analysis:
In the Rajya Sabha on 3 December 2009, Jairam Ramesh said there was no question of India accepting a legally binding emission reduction cut. He said India would accept international verification of reductions only if supported by finance and technology transfers.

The Copenhagen Accord was noted by the Conference of Parties on 18 December 2009. In January 2010 the UNFCCC clarified that the Accord was a political document and not legally binding. India associated itself with the Accord but did not take on binding emission targets.

The statement held for the Copenhagen round.
